articles.title: India's First Portable Petrol-Powered EV Charger Is Here To Fight Range Anxiety - Cartoq
articles.content: A lot of people do not want to buy electric cars for long-distance travelling because of range anxiety. The main reason is that the charging infrastructure on Indian roads is not very reliable. So, to help in solving the issue of range anxiety, recently a company named Rebel Power has done something unique. It has launched its specialised portable 5kVA petrol-powered EV charger so that EV owners can take their vehicles on long road trips without worrying about the range. The video showing this portable petrol-powered EV charger has been shared on Instagram by Rebel Power India on their channel. It starts off with the presenter mentioning that they have launched India's first portable 5kVA EV charger, which only weighs 27 kg. Following this, he then adds that this charger can be easily fitted in the trunk of the vehicle and can be taken on long-distance trips without worrying about the range of the vehicle. After the introduction, the presenter mentions that this particular charger can be turned on by pulling on the recoil starter. He then shows the charger being connected to a bulb setup, which glows constantly. He adds that the vehicle can be charged using the constant 19A current. Now, coming to the detailed specifications of the Rebel Power 5kVA EV charger. Basically, it is a petrol-powered generator and not a charger. It has been designed as an emergency off-grid power backup for electric vehicle owners. The company has mainly designed it to address range anxiety during long-distance travel. It can be useful for roadside assistance (RSA) teams, fleet operators and highway breakdown patrols. It is currently available online for a price of Rs 63,499. The RP EV-C50i is a single-phase portable generator that can deliver up to 5,000 Watts (5kVA) with a constant 19A AC current output. This generator can be connected to modern 3-wheeler and 4-wheeler EVs using their standard Type-2 portable charger or charging brick. The company claims that it can fully charge a 30 kWh EV battery in around 7.5 hours. It uses inverter technology with a claimed THD of below 2 percent to provide pure sine wave power. Meanwhile, its 6-litre petrol tank offers around five hours of continuous operation at a fuel consumption of approximately 1.3 litres per hour. As mentioned, it weighs 27 kg and can be carried in the boot, and it comes with a 2-year manufacturer warranty. For charging, the generator setup requires a neutral-ground bond or suitable earthing arrangement for the EV to recognise a safe electrical connection. This particular petrol-powered generator may look ironic to a lot of people. However, it has to be mentioned that the use case that it has makes it a viable option. It has mainly been designed for EV owners who use their electric vehicles for long road trips or travel to remote locations where electricity and charging infrastructure both are very scarce. articles.title: Tata Steel Commissions India's First Coke Oven Gas Injection Project - Construction World
articles.content: COG is a hydrogen- and hydrocarbon-rich byproduct of coke production. It contains more than 55 per cent hydrogen and methane and is typically used for power generation, heating or flaring. Under the new project, the gas is cleaned to remove harmful tar and sulphur before being piped into the blast furnace through small nozzles known as tuyeres. The project was implemented with technology partner Paul Wurth-SMS and equipment supplier Kobelco. By injecting COG into the furnace, Tata Steel is using hydrogen in the gas as a chemical reducer, partially replacing carbon-based inputs and lowering the quantity of metallurgical coke or coal required to produce iron. The company said the system could provide a three-fuel operating model for the blast furnace, combining conventional fuels with internally generated process gas. This is expected to improve operational flexibility and efficiency while providing a relatively direct way to reduce emissions without fundamentally changing the blast-furnace process. Tata Steel said the project forms part of its wider decarbonisation and technology investment programme. In FY26, the company recorded consolidated carbon dioxide emission intensity of 2.22 tonnes per tonne of crude steel and reported R&D expenditure of Rs. 14.56 bn. The Meramandali facility, formerly known as Bhushan Steel, became part of Tata Steel after Bamnipal Steel completed its acquisition in 2018. The plant is described as one of India’s leading integrated steel facilities and the country’s largest producer of auto-grade steel. Tata Steel has commissioned India’s first coke oven gas (COG) injection project at its Meramandali steel plant in Odisha’s Dhenkanal district. The initiative is intended to reduce fossil-fuel consumption and carbon emissions from conventional blast-furnace ironmaking while improving the use of gases generated within the integrated steel plant.
